name: integration-tier-pure
body:
An integration test exercises TWO OR MORE units TOGETHER — the wiring between them — with everything ELSE faked. Its collaborators outside the units under test (filesystem, database, git, process spawning, network, clock, environment) are in-memory fakes; the test performs NO real I/O.

The boundary is identical to the unit tier: an integration test is still pure in-memory — no temp directory, no `db.lbug` open, no git invocation, no process spawn. The only difference from unit is the unit count: two or more real (in-memory) units collaborating, with the rest faked.

AC: an integration test's body takes no real-I/O action; the units under test are the real in-memory implementations, every other collaborator is faked; running the test creates and leaves no filesystem artifacts.
